value.body: A drug safety associate records and assesses reports of side effects from medicines. Pharmaceutical companies and the service firms that run safety work for them are the main employers. A typical day involves reading case reports, entering them into a safety database, coding them, and checking them against reporting timelines.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Pharm, M.Pharm or Pharm.D; some employers also take life sciences or nursing graduates

items.label: India's programme
items.value: Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI), run by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers are usually hired straight after a pharmacy degree into case processing roles, often through campus drives or walk-ins. A short course in pharmacovigilance can help but is not always required. Attention to detail and clear English writing matter in the selection tests.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common path: drug safety associate → senior associate → safety scientist or aggregate reports roles.
Early work is repetitive and target-driven.
Some roles involve shifts to match overseas clients.
Jobs are concentrated in cities with pharma and service hubs.
